focus: Paired Central Texas vine-ID lesson: Passifloraceae/Passiflora versus Vitaceae/Vitis

Passifloraceae.where_to_look_first: Go to a node and locate the tendril: in local Passiflora the tendril is axillary, arising beside the leaf/flower axis. Then inspect the flower for the corona and elevated reproductive column.
core_characters: Climbing herbs or vines with axillary tendrils in Passiflora.
Leaves alternate, often lobed; stipules present; petiole or leaf base may carry nectary glands depending on species.
Flowers usually show 5 sepals + 5 petals (petals sometimes absent in some family members) and a conspicuous extrastaminal corona.
Stamens and ovary are elevated on a gynophore/androgynophore.
Passiflora usually has 3 styles/stigmas prominently displayed above the stamens.
Ovary superior and one-locular with parietal placentation.
Fruit berry-like or capsular; seeds often arillate.

Vitaceae.where_to_look_first: Go to a node and look directly opposite the leaf: Vitis commonly places a tendril or inflorescence leaf-opposed, not in the leaf axil.
core_characters: Usually woody climbers/lianas with leaf-opposed tendrils.
Leaves alternate and stipulate; simple or compound, often lobed/toothed.
Flowers are small and actinomorphic, unlike showy passionflowers.
Petals are 4–5 and in Vitis often cohere and fall as a cap/calyptre.

tie_breaker.node_level: Passiflora tendril = axillary; Vitis tendril/inflorescence = opposite the leaf.
tie_breaker.flower_level: Passiflora = corona + elevated androgynophore + 3 prominent stigmas; Vitis = tiny flowers, no passionflower corona, petals often shed as a cap.
tie_breaker.fruit_level: Both can produce berries, so berry fruit alone is not a good family separator.

cards.look_here_first: At a node, find the single axillary tendril beside the leaf/flower. On the flower, find the two rings/series of corona filaments and the central elevated reproductive column.
confirm: Perennial climber with one axillary unbranched tendril per node in detailed Central Texas descriptions.
Leaves alternate and 3-lobed in local var. glabriflora descriptions.
Five sepals and five petals surround multiple corona-filament series.
Five stamens and the ovary/styles are elevated on a central column.
Fruit is borne from the same axillary floral system and contains multiple seeds.

cards.look_here_first: Use the Passiflora node first—axillary tendril—then inspect the unusually narrow/deeply divided leaf lobes before moving to flower details.
confirm: Hays-local Passiflora anchor in the Master Plant Pool.
Keep family confirmation structural: axillary tendril + Passiflora flower architecture.
Leaf shape is useful at species level but must not substitute for family confirmation.

cards.look_here_first: Inspect one node: the tendril is paired with the leaf 180 degrees opposite it. Then flip the leaf over and look for the dense white woolly underside.
confirm: Woody liana, often covering shrubs and small trees.
Tendril at the node is leaf-opposed and typically forked.
Leaves alternate and highly variable in lobing.
Lower leaf surface is densely white woolly/tomentose, producing a conspicuously two-colored leaf.
Inflorescence can replace the tendril and is likewise leaf-opposed rather than axillary.
